summary:
# NOTES: "TOMMY" by Joseph Hocking (single book; no BOOK headings)

## Front matter
- Title page: *Tommy*, by Joseph Hocking, author of "All for a Scrap of Paper," "Dearer than Life." Publisher: Hodder and Stoughton, London/New York/Toronto, MCMXVI (1916).
- Other Hocking titles listed: Facing Fearful Odds; O'er Moor and Fen; The Wilderness; Rosaleen O'Hara; The Soul of Dominie Wildthorne; Follow the Gleam; David Baring; The Trampled Cross.
- Author's Note (Feb 1916, Priors' Corner, Totteridge, Herts): author met "Tommy" before enlistment during 6+ months of recruiting meetings; visited camps, France and Flanders (La Bassee, Neuve Chapelle, Ypres, front trenches <100 yards from German sandbags). Says only part is imagination; nearly every incident told by Tommy himself; tale is fact. Dedicated to soldiers, parents, loved ones.

## CHAPTER I (Sunday, first Sunday in June 1914; Brunford, Lancashire cotton town)
- 3:30 pm, Tom Pollard leaves home in Dixon Street for the Thorn and Thistle public-house. Crosses tram lines in St. George's Street; Liverpool Road.
- Polly (Polly Powell): buxom, bold-eyed, red-cheeked, ~24, daughter of landlord Enoch Powell. Highly coloured dress, big feathers. Says "You're late, Tom." Rival admirers: Jim Scott, Jim Dixon, young landlord at the Bull and Butcher.
- Tom says he has an "appointment." Polly guesses Alice Lister. Polly claims father thinks Tom has brains; Tom took three prizes at Mechanics' Institute last winter; father would fund a small mill ("you'd make brass"). Tom has no capital. Polly invites him back to tea; Jim Dixon coming to tea that evening.
- Tom's background: parents weavers (father 30 shillings/week); Tom promised a Tackler's job. Gave up Sunday School; frequent at Thorn and Thistle.
- Alice Lister: ~20, refined, intelligent; father a small manufacturer (once weaver), "doin' vary weel"; mother. Alice sang contralto, pianist, French/German classes, lover of books. Attends Young Men's Class/Sunday School (Brunford's Sunday schools).
- Emily Bilson mocks Tom; girls gossip (Polly, Bull and Butcher landlord).
- Alice's ultimatum on Liverpool Road / Scott's Park: give up Alice or give up Thorn and Thistle. Tom: "religious lolly-pops"; "Methody parson." Alice: "Duty, God." Tom mentions Harry Briarfield at Alice's house for supper.
- Harry Waterman (tall, handsome, florid, light-brown hair; claims son of a Warwickshire squire; trained in Germany; "not up to Alice's mark" in Tom's view). Invites Tom to club at Rose and Crown at seven; had mocked religion.
- Tom chooses Waterman/Polly. Alice: "I see that your choice is made." Alice leaves. Tom goes to tea with Polly.
- Home: Mother (Mrs. Martha Pollard) scolds; "Bein' fools runs in the family."

## CHAPTER II
- Brunford: trade boom; drunkenness with big wages. Tom's coarse drift; Jim Parkin reports Tom spent four shillings at Thorn and Thistle.
- July 1914: Austria's ultimatum to Serbia; Sir Edward Grey. Manufacturers' talk of German trade rivalry.
- Enoch Powell: "six weeks" for Germans. Liège held out.
- Lord Kitchener's call for half a million men.
- Waterman, back from absence, says he will get commission; says English will never lick Germans.
- Mr. Shweitzer, German resident of Brunford, farewell dinner at Bull and Butcher; says Kaiser will rule England; an Englishman punches him, breaking his jaw.
- Elijah Butterworth (three sons in army) challenges Tom. Tom says "Let 'em join if they want to."
- Winter 1914-15: frostbite, stalemate. Tom attends recruiting meetings.
- New Year (1915): big recruiting meeting, Mechanics' Institute great hall; speaker describes Belgium atrocities. Tom: "By God! I can't stand this!" Speaker: "Who will be the first?" Tom: "No! By God, no!" gives his name. "Thus Tom became a soldier."
- Mother: "Ay, tha mun be sent to Lancaster asylum." Footnote: incident of Lancashire city German dinner occurred.

## CHAPTER III
- Polly at midnight: "Thou'st noan been such a fool?" Tom: "I couldn't help it." Polly: "Of course I'll be true to you."
- Next morning Tom meets Alice near Town Hall; she says "it was splendid of you." Tom: "I have heard there is a young parson going after you."
- Joins Loyal North Lancashires (unnamed battalion); camp in Lancashire town ~30 miles from Brunford. Drunk and disorderly; punished.
- Robert Penrose: young Cornish gentleman ranker (Charterhouse, Godalming); best boxer; urges Tom to Y.M.C.A. Tom mocks "religious lolly-pops."
- Alec McPhail: tall Scot, Black Watch (kilts; mother godly, U.P. Kirk elder father; Ingersoll reading; Shorter Catechism). Meets "wee lassie" named Alice (unknown). Tom: "I wur a bit in the religious line myself once."
- Colonel: "Why did you make a beast of yourself?" Suggests Y.M.C.A. hall. Penrose: "kicked out of the Army."
- Tom goes to Y.M.C.A. (concerts, recitations, French class, writing room). French verbs: je suis, vous etes, nous sommes, ils sont.
- Leave in Brunford; Polly serves beer; Tom drinks. Polly's dresses highly coloured.
- Move south: Euston to Waterloo; drunk men. Surrey camp near Godalming (Charterhouse visible). Penrose later commissioned; Tom sees Lt. Waterman in Surrey camp: "I didn't expect to meet Waterman here."

## CHAPTER IV
- Surrey camp: nearly 30,000 men; six Y.M.C.A. huts. Tom's French report. Tom says "Y.M.C.A. is a fair God-send."
- Mother's letter: Polly walking out with Jim Dixon; Polly "just the image of her mother"; signs "Mrs. Martha Pollard"; postscript about German Emperor.
- Alec McPhail drinks, admits fear; "It's either whisky or releegion."
- Embarkation at Folkestone; Boulogne; troop train; march; guns booming. Tom: "I wonder now——"
- Farewell meeting at Y.M.C.A.: speaker (unnamed) on the "Great Unknown," personal Saviour. McPhail and Tom to canteen; McPhail gives heart to God. Tom: "I'm noan going to turn religious... but he's got the reight on't."

## CHAPTER V
- Ypres salient. Sergeant Ashworth (20 years' service; wounded twice) describes battle of Wipers, Cloth Hall, Cathedral, poison gas, German surrender trick.
- Tom in trenches (Piccadilly, Haymarket, Bond Street, Whitehall = trench names). Lancashire lad shot through head looking over sandbags.
- Bombardment; counterattack; young officer rescues wounded German who shoots him dead. Tom's change: sees heroism; religion's power.
- Waterman as staff officer: "Ah, is that you, Pollard?"
- Night sentry duty; Tom's prayer "O God!" Thinks of Jim Bates, Arthur Wadge, Bill Perkins, George Wilson (dead pals).

## CHAPTER VI
- Alice's night: Harry Briarfield (24, partner in father George Briarfield's firm; Sunday School teacher; war contracts); proposes. Mr. George Lister, Mrs. Lister. Alice's earlier refusal of Mr. Skelton (young minister). Alice cannot decide; prays "O God, save him!" at midnight (same time as Tom's prayer).

## CHAPTER VII
- ~1 am: German voice: "you Lancashires are going to attack us at six o'clock to-morrow morning, eleven hundred strong." Tom reports to subaltern; Colonel; attack repelled with Black Watch reinforcement. Colonel Blount (Lancashires); Major Blundell.
- Tom's conversion: "he felt the reality of God."
- Alec McPhail wounded; Tom visits hospital; nurse; McPhail dies: "It's a' richt." Tom sings "Jesu, Lover of my soul"; both recite Psalm 23.

## CHAPTER VIII
- Colonel Blount and Major Blundell; General Withers; Brigadier. Achan/treachery.
- Tom sees Waterman with staff officers near Potijze Road/Water Tower.
- Night: Waterman throws paper with signal toward German lines. Tom attacks him; Lt. Penrose arrives; Jackson takes revolver. Tom crawls into no-man's-land, wrestles German, breaks his shoulder blade, retrieves paper; wounded (left arm, right shoulder) by German fire. Nick (Brunford friend): "Ay, Tom, tha'st done a good neet's work."
- Colonel Blount visits Tom; mentions D.C.M.

## CHAPTER IX
- Court martial: Waterman admits he is German (parents spelled name German fashion, two n's — "Waterman" vs German spelling); "I have counted the cost." Shot at dawn against a wall. Tom recommended for D.C.M.

## CHAPTER X
- Late November: newspapers "Heroism of a Lancashire Lad." Mrs. Pollard: "Our Tom an 'ero, eh?" Ezekiel Pollard (father).
- December leave: Tom arrives Brunford Saturday (went through London, King's Cross). Parents at station; crowd cheers. Polly at station; Tom refuses her invitation to Thorn and Thistle; says he is teetotal "following the example of the King."
- Family kneels in prayer.

## CHAPTER XI
- Sunday: Tom attends chapel with parents. Meets Alice in vestibule; walks home up Liverpool Road into quiet lane. Alice never engaged to Harry Briarfield or to the young parson. "I can't help waiting for you." Tom promises to work for her.
- George Lister: "our Alice is a fool" — then approves. Mrs. Lister: "yon's a grand lad."
- Alice and George accompany Tom to Waterloo; author saw him off. Tom: "It's only au revoir as the French say." Kipling's "ship that found herself" book lent to Tom. Alice: "I shall be loving you."
- Ends: Tom waves from train; "God help me to do my bit, and then take me back to her."
